Nicole Kidman played the role of Nala in the 1994 Disney animated film "The Lion King." She was the first Australian actress to voice a Disney princess. The role was originally offered to Madonna, but she turned it down. Other notable actresses who were considered for the part included Whitney Houston, Angela Lansbury, and Whoopi Goldberg. Kidman's performance as Nala was well-received by critics and audiences alike, and she received an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress for her work in the film.

Nicole Kidman played the role of Simba in the 2004 Disney animated film "The Lion King." She also appeared as Nala in the 2019 live-action adaptation of the film, which is directed by Jon Favreau and produced by Disney+.

Nicole Kidman played the role of Sarabi, the graceful and wise lioness who is Simba's mother, in "The Lion King." Her portrayal added a layer of elegance and depth to the character, highlighting Sarabi's strength and compassion as she navigated the challenges facing the pride with dignity.
